name: New Incentives: cash incentives for routine childhood vaccination in northern Nigeria
summary: New Incentives pays caregivers in eleven states of northern Nigeria small cash incentives (about ₦8,700, under $6, per infant in 2025) for bringing infants to government clinics for BCG, Penta, PCV and measles vaccines. For 2025 (audited spending $26.9 million, 1.85 million infants enrolled) we estimate deaths averted cause by cause, from a 2017-2020 randomised trial's coverage gains, Bauchi's GBD death risks and each vaccine's efficacy, plus hepatitis B deaths in adulthood, a little later income and the cash itself: about 14 years of healthy life per $1,000. The biggest uncertainties are how far the trial's gains carry to today's areas and death rates, and the credit shared with Gavi and the Nigerian government, who pay for the vaccines and health workers (New Incentives is credited with about half).

sections.explainer: What the intervention does for each unit reached, from the best available studies, before any adjustment.

sections.title: Adjustments
sections.explainer: Discounts for weaker evidence, what would have happened anyway, credit shared with others, and delivery falling short. All multiply the outcome.

sections.explainer: Staff who earn less than they could elsewhere pay part of the cost in kind. With credit by share of resources, your dollar is credited with its share of the full cost only.

rows.explainer: Programme-service expenses for calendar 2025 from the audited consolidated statements (New Incentives and its Nigerian subsidiary All Babies Are Equal Initiative). The programme is one activity: cash incentives at government immunisation sessions, with the awareness work and vaccine-supply support that go with it. The oral rehydration salts pilot started in May 2025 (41,000 sachets in 43 clinics of one LGA) is under 1% of spending and isn't split out or modelled.

rows.label: Programme expenses (all programmes), 2025

source.title: New Incentives and Subsidiary, Audited Consolidated Financial Statements, December 31, 2025 (CohnReznick)

rows.explainer: Programme-service expenses for 2025; the same figure as program_spend, since the whole programme is modelled.

rows.label: Overhead multiplier (total ÷ program expenses)
rows.explainer: Spreads management and fundraising over programs in proportion to their cost, as GiveWell and ACE do.

rows.label: Cost of the modelled program, including overhead
Infants newly enrolled in 2025

source.title: New Incentives, Annual Report 2025

rows.explainer: New Incentives' own count of infants enrolled at its 7,189 clinics in 11 northern Nigerian states in 2025 (administrative data, checked by unannounced visits to 14% of disbursement sessions). Total expenses over this count is $14.57 per infant, close to the charity's own $14.80 (it divides the unaudited $27.3 million).

rows.label: Enrolled infants as a share of all children born in the clinics' catchment areas
rows.explainer: The trial's effect is an average over every child in a clinic's catchment area (intention to treat), enrolled or not, so the effect applies to the whole birth cohort, not only to enrolled infants. Our judgment of the share enrolled: at the 24-month coverage surveys 65% of 6-12-month-olds had had any vaccine (zero-dose 35%) and 68% BCG (coverage report, Tables 5 and 8); nearly every vaccinated child in a programme area is vaccinated at a programme clinic, but some at campaigns or other clinics. Range 50-80%. A lower share means more children reached per enrolled infant, so a higher result.

rows.label: Children born in the programme clinics' catchment areas in 2025
rows.explainer: Infants enrolled divided by the enrolled share: the population the trial's coverage effects apply to.

rows.label: Cost per child in the catchment areas
rows.explainer: Context: the cost per child the coverage effects are averaged over.

rows.label: Cost per infant enrolled
rows.explainer: Context: the charity reports $14.80 for 2025 (total expenses over infants served, unaudited expenses).

rows.label: Years of protection counted (birth to age five)
rows.explainer: The vaccines protect through early childhood; the deaths counted below are those before age five (the GBD risks are chances of dying before five), with the few later deaths added as a ratio. 60 months, the site's shared figure.

rows.label: Increase in BCG coverage (trial)

source.title: IDinsight, Impact of Conditional Cash Transfers on Routine Childhood Immunizations: Evidence from North West Nigeria (evaluation brief, 2020)

rows.explainer: IDinsight's cluster-randomised trial (167 clinics in Katsina, Zamfara and Jigawa, endline Nov 2019-Feb 2020, 5,173 children aged 12-16 months): caregiver-reported, cross-checked against cards and clinic registers, treatment minus control. 95% CI as the range.

rows.label: Increase in first-dose Penta (and PCV) coverage (trial)

source.title: IDinsight, Impact of Conditional Cash Transfers on Routine Childhood Immunizations: Evidence from North West Nigeria (evaluation brief, 2020)

rows.explainer: Same trial. PCV is given at the same visits as Penta, so its doses rise with Penta's (the coverage report tracks only Penta for this reason). 95% CI as the range.

rows.label: Increase in first-dose measles coverage (trial)

source.title: IDinsight, Impact of Conditional Cash Transfers on Routine Childhood Immunizations: Evidence from North West Nigeria (evaluation brief, 2020)

rows.explainer: Same trial, 95% CI as the range. Campaigns gave measles vaccine in the study areas just before endline (brief p. 4), so this routine-dose effect may understate the routine programme's effect where campaigns are rarer.

rows.label: Rise in first-dose Penta coverage after rollout (coverage surveys, no control)

source.title: New Incentives, Measuring Change in Childhood Immunization Coverage Before and After New Incentives' Program: Baseline, Follow-ups for Cohorts 1-8, 11 (coverage report 2024)

rows.explainer: New Incentives' coverage monitoring, nine cohorts in Bauchi, Katsina, Sokoto and Jigawa, baseline vs 24 months after rollout (3,734 and 4,102 surveys), pooled. Pre-post, so it includes the background trend; used only for the ratio between doses, which the trial's public brief doesn't report.

rows.label: Rise in second-dose Penta coverage after rollout (coverage surveys, no control)

source.title: New Incentives, Measuring Change in Childhood Immunization Coverage Before and After New Incentives' Program: Baseline, Follow-ups for Cohorts 1-8, 11 (coverage report 2024)

rows.explainer: Same survey and table: pooled change from baseline to 24 months.

rows.label: Rise in third-dose Penta coverage after rollout (coverage surveys, no control)

source.title: New Incentives, Measuring Change in Childhood Immunization Coverage Before and After New Incentives' Program: Baseline, Follow-ups for Cohorts 1-8, 11 (coverage report 2024)

rows.explainer: Same survey and table: pooled change from baseline (26.9%) to 24 months (54.1%).

rows.label: Increase in second-dose Penta and PCV coverage
rows.explainer: The trial's first-dose effect scaled by the surveys' ratio of second-dose to first-dose rises.

rows.label: Increase in third-dose Penta and PCV coverage
rows.explainer: The trial's first-dose effect scaled by the surveys' ratio of third-dose to first-dose rises (22.5 points). Consistent with the trial's 27-point rise in full immunisation, which needs the third dose.

rows.label: Increase in Penta protection, weighting each dose by the protection it adds
rows.explainer: The share of a three-dose course's protection that the first, second and third doses give (the site's shared figures: 35%, 55%, 10%) times each dose's coverage increase.

rows.label: Increase in PCV protection, weighting each dose by the protection it adds
rows.explainer: As for Penta, with the site's shared PCV dose shares; PCV doses are given at the Penta visits.

rows.label: Share of the Penta rise that also brings rotavirus vaccine

source.title: UNICEF data warehouse: WHO/UNICEF estimates of national immunization coverage (WUENIC), Nigeria, IM_ROTAC and IM_DTP3

rows.explainer: Rotavirus vaccine is given at the 6- and 10-week visits since Nigeria introduced it in September 2022 (coverage report, footnote 4); it isn't a condition for the incentive, but in the trial the vaccines given at the same visits without an incentive rose about as much as the incentivised ones (brief p. 4). WHO and UNICEF's estimates for Nigeria in 2025: last-dose rotavirus 47% against DTP3 62%, a ratio of 0.76; 2024 54 against 63 (0.86), the high end. The low end allows for northern states below the national ratio. The 2023-24 DHS's much lower rotavirus coverage is for children mostly born before the rollout.

rows.label: Increase in rotavirus vaccine protection
rows.explainer: The Penta protection increase times the share of those visits that give rotavirus vaccine.

rows.label: Measles vaccine efficacy in Nigeria
rows.explainer: The site's shared blend: Fowotade et al. 2015 and Uzicanin and Zimmerman 2011 weighted 35% each, the rest on the efficacy implied by IDinsight's biomarker pilot in northern Nigeria (all shared facts).

rows.label: Measles vaccine efficacy in the literature (without the Nigerian biomarker result)
rows.explainer: The two literature figures alone, with their shared weights; compared with the blend above it gives the discount for vaccine effectiveness in this setting.

rows.label: Effectiveness of the other vaccines in this setting, relative to their trials
rows.explainer: Cold chain and handling that weaken measles vaccine in northern Nigeria weaken the others too: the site's shared share (75%) of the measles discount applies to every other vaccine's efficacy.

rows.label: PCV efficacy against pneumococcal disease of all serotypes

source.title: Cochrane review CD004977, Pneumococcal conjugate vaccines for preventing vaccine-type invasive pneumococcal disease and X-ray defined pneumonia in children less than two years of age

rows.explainer: Cochrane review of PCV trials (Lucero et al.): pooled efficacy against invasive pneumococcal disease of all serotypes in HIV-negative children under two, 95% CI as the range. All serotypes, since pneumococcal deaths include those the vaccine doesn't cover.

rows.label: Share of under-five pneumonia deaths caused by pneumococcus

source.title: GBD 2016 Lower Respiratory Infections Collaborators, Lancet Infect Dis 2018;18:1191-1210

rows.explainer: GBD 2016's aetiology: 341,029 of 652,572 under-five LRI deaths caused by pneumococcus (52%), its uncertainty interval as the range. The latest published round with an under-five pneumococcal figure that we could read.

rows.label: Hib vaccine efficacy against Hib disease

source.title: Swingler G, Fransman D, Hussey G, Conjugate vaccines for preventing Haemophilus influenzae type B infections, Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2007 (CD001729.pub2)
source.quote: The relative risk for invasive Hib disease was 0.20 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.07 to 0.54

rows.explainer: Cochrane review of Hib conjugate vaccine trials (Swingler, Fransman and Hussey 2007; the 2009 update was withdrawn): relative risk of invasive Hib disease 0.20 (0.07-0.54), so efficacy 80% (46-93%).

rows.label: Efficacy of three doses of whole-cell pertussis vaccine (in Penta)

source.title: Cochrane review CD001478.pub6, Acellular vaccines for preventing whooping cough in children

rows.explainer: Our judgment anchored on the Cochrane review of whole-cell pertussis vaccines (efficacy of the better whole-cell vaccines in the 80-90% range; deaths, the severe end, are prevented at least as well). 85%, range 70-94%.

rows.label: Efficacy of three doses of diphtheria toxoid (in Penta)

source.title: WHO, Diphtheria vaccine: WHO position paper, August 2017 (Weekly Epidemiological Record 92(31))

rows.explainer: Our judgment anchored on WHO's diphtheria position paper (2017), which cites effectiveness of a primary series in the high 80s to 90s. 87%, range 70-97%.

rows.label: Efficacy of three doses of tetanus toxoid against post-neonatal tetanus

source.title: WHO, Tetanus vaccines: WHO position paper, February 2017 (Weekly Epidemiological Record 92(6))

rows.explainer: Our judgment: tetanus toxoid is among the most effective vaccines (WHO position paper 2017). 95%, range 80-100%. Only post-neonatal tetanus counts; newborn tetanus is prevented by vaccinating mothers.

rows.label: BCG efficacy against tuberculosis deaths before age five

source.title: Trunz BB, Fine P, Dye C, Effect of BCG vaccination on childhood tuberculous meningitis and miliary tuberculosis worldwide, Lancet 2006;367:1173-80

rows.explainer: Our judgment anchored on Trunz, Fine and Dye (Lancet 2006): BCG at birth gives consistently high protection against tuberculous meningitis and miliary TB in young children (about three-quarters), less against pulmonary TB. 60%, range 40-80%.

rows.label: Rotavirus vaccine efficacy against rotavirus deaths
rows.explainer: The site's shared figure (the LiST meta-analysis).

rows.label: Share of under-five pneumonia deaths after the age for Penta and PCV
rows.explainer: Bauchi, GBD 2021 (shared facts): under-five pneumonia deaths minus first-week and 7-27-day deaths, minus the deaths between one month and six weeks (the shared ratio to neonatal deaths).

rows.label: Share of under-five meningitis deaths after the age for Penta and PCV
rows.explainer: Same method with the shared Bauchi meningitis deaths.

rows.label: Share of under-five tetanus deaths after the age for Penta
rows.explainer: Same method with the shared Bauchi tetanus deaths: most under-five tetanus deaths are newborn tetanus, which infant vaccination can't prevent.

rows.label: Share of under-five rotavirus deaths after the age for rotavirus vaccine
rows.explainer: Same method with the shared Bauchi rotavirus deaths.

rows.label: Share of under-five measles deaths after the age for measles vaccine (9 months)
rows.explainer: Shared figures: the share of infant measles deaths before nine months times Bauchi's infant measles deaths, out of its under-five measles deaths.

rows.label: Chance of dying of rotavirus diarrhoea before age five, Bauchi
rows.explainer: Bauchi's chance of dying of pneumonia before five, scaled by its rotavirus deaths over its pneumonia deaths (all shared GBD 2021 facts for the same population).

rows.label: Death risk from these causes in the programme's states today, relative to Bauchi in 2021
rows.explainer: Our judgment. The programme's 2025 enrolments are about 70% in North West states (Kano, Katsina, Jigawa, Kebbi, Sokoto, Zamfara, Kaduna), where the 2023-24 DHS puts under-five mortality at 140 per 1,000 against 127 in the North East (Bauchi, Gombe, Yobe): about 5% above Bauchi's zone. Child mortality has been falling a few percent a year since 2021, about 10% by 2025. Net 0.95, range 0.75-1.2.

rows.label: Death risk from these causes for a child the programme gets vaccinated, relative to the average child
rows.explainer: The GBD risks are averages over children of whom a quarter to a half are already vaccinated (baseline Penta 3 27%, BCG 46%, measles 26%: coverage report Table 5); an unvaccinated child's risk from the vaccine-preventable part is higher by 1 / (1 - coverage x efficacy), about 1.05-1.15 by vaccine. The marginal child is mostly one who completes the series rather than a zero-dose child (the trial found any-injectable coverage similar in both arms, brief p. 4), so no extra for poverty. Our judgment 1.05, range 1-1.15.

rows.label: Combined scaling of the Bauchi 2021 risks
rows.explainer: The two scalings together.

rows.label: Pneumonia deaths averted before five per child in the catchment areas
rows.formula: @givewell_common.bauchi_death_risk_pneumonia_under_5 * pneumonia_post_schedule_share * (pneumococcal_share_of_pneumonia * pcv_efficacy * pcv_protection_increase + @givewell_common.proportion_of_lower_respiratory_infection_deaths_caused * hib_efficacy * penta_protection_increase) * other_vaccine_setting_adj * risk_scale
rows.explainer: Chance of dying of pneumonia before five (Bauchi) x share after the vaccine age x (pneumococcal share x PCV efficacy x PCV protection increase + Hib share x Hib efficacy x Penta protection increase) x the setting discount x the risk scaling.

rows.label: Meningitis deaths averted before five per child
rows.formula: @givewell_common.both_under_5_meningitis_2021 * meningitis_post_schedule_share * (@givewell_common.proportion_of_meningitis_deaths_caused_by_path_0_2672 * @givewell_common.adjustment_for_alignment_with_pneumococcal_meningitis_b * pcv_efficacy * pcv_protection_increase + @givewell_common.proportion_of_meningitis_deaths_caused_by_pathogens_add * @givewell_common.adjustment_for_alignment_with_hib_meningitis_burden_est * hib_efficacy * penta_protection_increase) * other_vaccine_setting_adj * risk_scale
rows.explainer: As for pneumonia, with the shared shares of meningitis deaths caused by Hib and pneumococcus, each times the shared factor aligning GBD's meningitis deaths with View-Hub's estimates.

rows.label: Whooping cough deaths averted before five per child
rows.explainer: Chance of dying of whooping cough before five x share after six weeks (the shared share of infant deaths before Penta age, applied to all under-five deaths, which slightly understates) x efficacy x Penta protection increase x setting x risk scaling.

rows.label: Diphtheria deaths averted before five per child
rows.explainer: As for whooping cough.

rows.label: Post-neonatal tetanus deaths averted before five per child
rows.explainer: As for whooping cough, counting only deaths after six weeks.

rows.label: Rotavirus deaths averted before five per child
rows.formula: rota_risk_under5 * rota_post_schedule_share * rotavirus_efficacy * rota_protection_increase * other_vaccine_setting_adj * risk_scale
rows.explainer: Chance of dying of rotavirus before five x share after the vaccine age x efficacy x rotavirus protection increase x setting x risk scaling.

rows.label: Measles deaths averted before five per child
rows.explainer: Chance of dying of measles before five x share after nine months x the Nigerian measles efficacy (already for this setting) x measles coverage increase x risk scaling.

rows.label: Tuberculosis deaths averted before five per child
rows.explainer: Chance of dying of tuberculosis before five x BCG efficacy x BCG coverage increase x setting x risk scaling.

rows.label: Deaths directly averted before five per child in the catchment areas
rows.formula: deaths_averted_pneumonia + deaths_averted_meningitis + deaths_averted_pertussis + deaths_averted_diphtheria + deaths_averted_tetanus + deaths_averted_rotavirus + deaths_averted_measles + deaths_averted_tb
rows.explainer: The sum over the vaccine-preventable causes.

rows.label: Deaths per child-year before five from the causes the vaccines prevent, without the programme
rows.explainer: Bauchi's GBD 2021 chances of dying before five of pneumonia, meningitis, whooping cough, diphtheria, tetanus, rotavirus diarrhoea, measles and tuberculosis (shared facts), times the scaling for today's states and for unvaccinated children, spread over the five years.

rows.label: Fall in deaths from these causes per child in the catchment areas
rows.explainer: Deaths averted per child over the deaths these causes would cause: the coverage increases times each vaccine's efficacy and the share of each cause it prevents. Built cause by cause above, since no trial measured the incentive's effect on deaths.

rows.label: Deaths indirectly caused by these diseases per direct death
rows.explainer: The site's shared figure for vaccine-preventable diseases (0.75): measles' immune suppression, and infections that leave children malnourished and open to other diseases, kill more than the deaths GBD codes to them. Check against all-cause mortality: the direct deaths alone for a child given the whole schedule (the rows below divided by each coverage increase) come to about 0.015 before five, about 15% of the post-neonatal under-five deaths in these zones (under-five mortality 127-140 per 1,000 in the 2023-24 DHS, roughly 40 of them neonatal); with the indirect ones about 27%, against an all-cause fall of 16% from PCV alone in the Gambian trial and larger falls after measles vaccination in observational studies. Our check, not a reason to change the shared figure.

rows.label: Chronic hepatitis B (HBsAg) prevalence, North West Nigeria

source.title: Ajuwon BI et al., Hepatitis B virus infection in Nigeria: a systematic review and meta-analysis of data published between 2010 and 2019, BMC Infect Dis 2021

rows.explainer: Ajuwon et al. 2021, systematic review and meta-analysis of 47 Nigerian studies (2010-2019): pooled 9.5%, North West the highest zone at 12.1% (95% CI 7.2-19.6%, the range).

rows.label: Share of chronic hepatitis B infections the infant series can prevent
rows.explainer: Our judgment: in West Africa most chronic infections come from horizontal transmission in early childhood, which the Penta series prevents; mother-to-child infections at birth need the birth dose (given at the BCG visit, so partly also raised). Anchor: the same review finds prevalence among people 17 and under (11.4%) close to adults', so infection is mostly acquired in childhood, before most mothers' carriage would explain it. 60%, range 40-80%.

rows.label: Share of chronic carriers who die prematurely of cirrhosis, liver failure or liver cancer

source.title: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine, A National Strategy for the Elimination of Hepatitis B and C: Phase Two Report (2017), Summary
source.quote: 15-25 percent of chronically infected persons will die prematurely

rows.explainer: National Academies (2017): 15-25% of chronically infected people die prematurely of these causes; the high end applies to infection in childhood (CDC puts it at about a quarter), so 25% best, range 15-25%. Treatment's future effect is in the shared expected-change adjustments of the adult bands.

rows.label: Share of chronically infected children who live to the ages liver disease kills
rows.explainer: Our judgment: in northern Nigeria a child who survives infancy has perhaps a 70% chance of reaching the 40s and 50s, when hepatitis B deaths peak. Range 50-90%.

rows.label: Hepatitis B vaccine efficacy against chronic infection (three doses)

source.title: WHO, Hepatitis B vaccines: WHO position paper, July 2017 (Weekly Epidemiological Record 92(27))

rows.explainer: Our judgment anchored on WHO's 2017 position paper (protection above 90% after a full series in infants). 90%, range 80-95%.

rows.label: Share of hepatitis B deaths at 15-49 (the rest at 50-74)
rows.explainer: Our judgment: in sub-Saharan Africa hepatitis B liver cancer is diagnosed young, mostly in the 30s to 50s, and cirrhosis deaths peak in the 40s and 50s. 45%, range 30-60%.

rows.label: Hepatitis B deaths averted in adulthood per child in the catchment areas
rows.formula: penta3_increase * hbsag_prevalence * hepb_share_after_infancy * hepb_death_share_of_carriers * hepb_survival_to_disease * hepb_efficacy * other_vaccine_setting_adj
rows.explainer: Third-dose Penta increase x prevalence x share preventable by the infant series x deaths among carriers x efficacy x the setting discount; split between the adult bands below, which add the shared expected fall in deaths and the discount for the wait.

rows.label: Deaths directly averted at ages 5-14 per child in the catchment areas
rows.formula: (@givewell_common.bauchi_death_risk_pneumonia_5_14 * (pneumococcal_share_of_pneumonia * pcv_efficacy * pcv_protection_increase + @givewell_common.proportion_of_lower_respiratory_infection_deaths_caused * hib_efficacy * penta_protection_increase) + @givewell_common.both_5_14_years_meningitis_2021 * (@givewell_common.proportion_of_meningitis_deaths_caused_by_path_0_2672 * @givewell_common.adjustment_for_alignment_with_pneumococcal_meningitis_b * pcv_efficacy * pcv_protection_increase + @givewell_common.proportion_of_meningitis_deaths_caused_by_pathogens_add * @givewell_common.adjustment_for_alignment_with_hib_meningitis_burden_est * hib_efficacy * penta_protection_increase) + (@givewell_common.both_5_14_years_pertussis_2021 * pertussis_efficacy + @givewell_common.both_5_14_years_diphtheria_2021 * diphtheria_efficacy + @givewell_common.both_5_14_years_tetanus_2021 * tetanus_efficacy) * penta_protection_increase + @givewell_common.both_5_14_years_tuberculosis_2021 * bcg_efficacy * rct_bcg_increase) * other_vaccine_setting_adj * risk_scale * (1 + @givewell_common.adjustment_for_reduction_in_vaccine_efficacy_over_time) * (1 + @givewell_common.adjustment_for_lower_vaccine_coverage_among_5_14_year_o) * (1 + @givewell_common.adjustment_for_expected_change_in_vaccine_preventable_d) + @givewell_common.both_5_14_years_measles_2021 * measles_efficacy * rct_measles_increase * risk_scale * (1 + @givewell_common.adjustment_for_reduction_in_vaccine_efficacy_over_time) * (1 + @givewell_common.adjustment_for_lower_vaccine_coverage_among_5_14_year_o) * (1 + @givewell_common.adjustment_for_expected_change_in_vaccine_preventable_d)
rows.explainer: Bauchi's GBD 2021 chances of dying at 5-14 of the same causes (shared facts), times the same pathogen shares, efficacies, coverage increases, setting discount and risk scaling as the under-five rows (no rotavirus: it kills young children), times the site's shared vaccine adjustments for this band: waning (-10%), lower past coverage in the GBD estimates, and the expected fall in these deaths.

rows.label: Years from vaccination to the middle of the deaths averted at 5-14
rows.explainer: Our judgment: ages 5-14 begin about five years after vaccination; their middle is about nine. Range 7-12.

rows.label: Deaths averted at 5-14, discounted to the age the under-five deaths are counted at
rows.explainer: Later deaths are further away: discounted at the shared rate for the years beyond the under-fives' midpoint.

rows.label: Deaths directly averted at ages 15-49 per child in the catchment areas
rows.formula: (@givewell_common.bauchi_death_risk_pneumonia_15_49 * (pneumococcal_share_of_pneumonia * pcv_efficacy * pcv_protection_increase + @givewell_common.proportion_of_lower_respiratory_infection_deaths_caused * hib_efficacy * penta_protection_increase) + @givewell_common.both_15_49_years_meningitis_2021 * (@givewell_common.proportion_of_meningitis_deaths_caused_by_path_0_2672 * @givewell_common.adjustment_for_alignment_with_pneumococcal_meningitis_b * pcv_efficacy * pcv_protection_increase + @givewell_common.proportion_of_meningitis_deaths_caused_by_pathogens_add * @givewell_common.adjustment_for_alignment_with_hib_meningitis_burden_est * hib_efficacy * penta_protection_increase) + (@givewell_common.both_15_49_years_pertussis_2021 * pertussis_efficacy + @givewell_common.both_15_49_years_diphtheria_2021 * diphtheria_efficacy + @givewell_common.both_15_49_years_tetanus_2021 * tetanus_efficacy) * penta_protection_increase + @givewell_common.both_15_49_years_tuberculosis_2021 * bcg_efficacy * rct_bcg_increase) * other_vaccine_setting_adj * risk_scale * (1 + @givewell_common.adjustment_for_reduction_in_bcg_vaccine_efficacy_over_t) * (1 + @givewell_common.adjustment_for_lower_vaccine_coverage_among_15_49_year) * (1 + @givewell_common.adjustment_for_expected_change_in_vaccine_prev_m0_3) + @givewell_common.both_15_49_years_measles_2021 * measles_efficacy * rct_measles_increase * risk_scale * (1 + @givewell_common.adjustment_for_reduction_in_bcg_vaccine_efficacy_over_t) * (1 + @givewell_common.adjustment_for_lower_vaccine_coverage_among_15_49_year) * (1 + @givewell_common.adjustment_for_expected_change_in_vaccine_prev_m0_3)
rows.explainer: Bauchi's GBD 2021 chances of dying at 15-49 of the same causes (shared facts), times the same pathogen shares, efficacies, coverage increases, setting discount and risk scaling as the under-five rows (no rotavirus: it kills young children), times the site's shared vaccine adjustments for this band: waning (the shared BCG figure, -80%, for every vaccine), lower past coverage in the GBD estimates, and the expected fall in these deaths.

rows.label: Years from vaccination to the middle of the deaths averted at 15-49
rows.explainer: Our judgment: the middle of ages 15-49 is about 32 years after vaccination; range 25-40.

rows.label: Deaths averted at 15-49, discounted to the age the under-five deaths are counted at
rows.explainer: Later deaths are further away: discounted at the shared rate for the years beyond the under-fives' midpoint.

rows.label: Deaths directly averted at ages 50-74 per child in the catchment areas
rows.formula: (@givewell_common.bauchi_death_risk_pneumonia_50_74 * (pneumococcal_share_of_pneumonia * pcv_efficacy * pcv_protection_increase + @givewell_common.proportion_of_lower_respiratory_infection_deaths_caused * hib_efficacy * penta_protection_increase) + @givewell_common.bauchi_death_risk_meningitis_50_74 * (@givewell_common.proportion_of_meningitis_deaths_caused_by_path_0_2672 * @givewell_common.adjustment_for_alignment_with_pneumococcal_meningitis_b * pcv_efficacy * pcv_protection_increase + @givewell_common.proportion_of_meningitis_deaths_caused_by_pathogens_add * @givewell_common.adjustment_for_alignment_with_hib_meningitis_burden_est * hib_efficacy * penta_protection_increase) + (@givewell_common.bauchi_death_risk_whooping_cough_50_74 * pertussis_efficacy + @givewell_common.bauchi_death_risk_diphtheria_50_74 * diphtheria_efficacy + @givewell_common.bauchi_death_risk_tetanus_50_74 * tetanus_efficacy) * penta_protection_increase + @givewell_common.bauchi_death_risk_tuberculosis_50_74 * bcg_efficacy * rct_bcg_increase) * other_vaccine_setting_adj * risk_scale * (1 + @givewell_common.adjustment_for_reduction_in_bcg_vaccine_effica_m0_9) * (1 + @givewell_common.adjustment_for_lower_vaccine_coverage_among_50_74_year) * (1 + @givewell_common.adjustment_for_expected_change_in_vaccine_prev_m0_6) + @givewell_common.bauchi_death_risk_measles_50_74 * measles_efficacy * rct_measles_increase * risk_scale * (1 + @givewell_common.adjustment_for_reduction_in_bcg_vaccine_effica_m0_9) * (1 + @givewell_common.adjustment_for_lower_vaccine_coverage_among_50_74_year) * (1 + @givewell_common.adjustment_for_expected_change_in_vaccine_prev_m0_6)
rows.explainer: Bauchi's GBD 2021 chances of dying at 50-74 of the same causes (shared facts), times the same pathogen shares, efficacies, coverage increases, setting discount and risk scaling as the under-five rows (no rotavirus: it kills young children), times the site's shared vaccine adjustments for this band: waning (the shared BCG figure, -90%, for every vaccine), lower past coverage in the GBD estimates, and the expected fall in these deaths.

source.quote: measles vaccination on average increases school grade attainment by 0.188 grades

rows.explainer: Anekwe et al. (Vaccine 2015), mother fixed effects in rural South Africa: measles vaccination raised grade attainment by 0.188 (95% CI 0.042-0.334). Observational, so discounted below.

rows.label: Rise in ln(earnings) per year of schooling
rows.explainer: Our judgment anchored on Montenegro and Patrinos (World Bank 2014), whose sub-Saharan average return to a year of schooling is about 12%; 10% for northern Nigeria's informal and farm economy, range 6-13%.

rows.label: Trust in the schooling effect as causal and as carrying over to Penta and PCV
rows.explainer: Our judgment: one observational study, of measles alone; we count it only for the measles coverage increase and halve it. Range 20-100%.

rows.label: Yearly increase in ln(consumption) in adulthood per child in the catchment areas
rows.explainer: Measles coverage increase x extra grades per vaccinated child x return per grade x the trust discount.

rows.explainer: Our estimate: vaccinated at 9 months, working from about 15-16 in rural northern Nigeria. Range 12-18.

rows.label: Later-life income gain per person reached, present value
rows.explainer: Discounted at the shared rate, the wait included, so the result moves with it. Never type in a present value worked out elsewhere: rebuild it from its inputs.

rows.explainer: The site's one figure (GiveWell's): an earner's income gain is shared with the household, so it counts this many times. Read by every model that values a long-term income gain (INV-13).

rows.explainer: Our judgment, against the template's 0.3 (0-0.9) for large cash injections into villages (Egger et al. 2022): small payments spread over many households move local markets less. 0.1, range 0-0.3.

rows.label: Child deaths averted by the cash, as a share of its consumption value
rows.explainer: Our judgment, against the template's 0.2 (0-0.5) for GiveDirectly; lower because the vaccines' own deaths averted are counted separately and the payments are small. 0.1, range 0-0.3.

rows.label: Trust in the trial's measured coverage effects
rows.explainer: The site's shared internal-validity figure for this trial, as the template prescribes for vaccination incentives. Context: a well-run cluster RCT with caregiver-reported coverage cross-checked against cards and registers; the coverage surveys' BCG-scar check rose more than reported BCG (28 against 22 points), which argues against over-reporting.

rows.label: How far the 2017-2020 trial effects carry to the 2025 programme
rows.explainer: Our judgment. For: the coverage surveys' pre-post rises in the 2022-2024 cohorts (Penta 1 +25, BCG +22, measles +18 points) exceed the trial's effects by about the background rise the trial's control arm showed, so the effect held up at scale and in new states. Against: the programme now runs in eleven states, some with higher baseline coverage, and the incentive is worth less: the trial paid about ₦766 per transfer (₦542 million over 708,000 transfers to December 2019, brief p. 2), about ₦2,700 in 2025 prices by the shared consumer price index, against ₦1,755 per transfer in 2025 (annual report p. 12), about two thirds as much. The 2025 annual report's newer cohorts (p. 23) are shown only as a chart. 0.85, range 0.65-1.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment (internal and external validity), a multiplier
rows.explainer: The product of its two parts.

rows.label: Share of the coverage gains that wouldn't have come anyway
rows.explainer: The trial's effects are already net of its control arm, so this only covers others who would have paid similar incentives in these areas without New Incentives (the National Cash Transfer Office and state governments are partners, none runs such a programme at this scale). 0.95, range 0.85-1.

rows.label: Gavi's and the government's cost per extra child vaccinated
rows.explainer: The vaccines, cold chain and health workers' time behind each extra vaccinated child are paid by Gavi and the Nigerian government, not by New Incentives: the site's shared figures.

rows.label: Partners' cost per child in the catchment areas
rows.explainer: Extra children vaccinated per child in the catchment areas (the third-dose increase, after the same evidence, counterfactual and implementation adjustments the outcome takes, so a shortfall isn't counted twice) times partners' cost per extra child.

rows.label: New Incentives' share of the resources behind the extra vaccinations
rows.explainer: Its cost per child over its own and its partners' cost per child (Convention 2: government and Gavi delivery at their cost).

rows.label: Share of credit used
rows.explainer: The charity's share of the resources behind the outcome; it applies whichever way credit is shared.

rows.label: Delivery at scale as in the trial
rows.explainer: Our judgment: 14% of disbursement sessions get unannounced visits and the scale-up's coverage surveys show rises as large as the trial's, but the reach is the charity's own count. 0.95, range 0.8-1.

rows.label: Others would have paid for this work anyway
rows.explainer: Our judgment: 68% of 2025 support came from one grantor and the charity holds over two years of spending in reserve with funding in place to 2028 (annual report p. 7), so a marginal gift partly frees its main funder's money for other work. 0.85, range 0.6-1, the low end of the template's 0.85-0.95 for top charities.
